title: Plan the week's lunches
recap: Pipo planned a veggie lunch week for Mia and Leo.
funFact: Agents like Meta's Muse can write emails for you, too. Next, Pipo answers Leo's teacher about the field trip!
postcard: Pipo packing colourful lunch boxes for two kids: {answer}
situation: School's back! Want me to plan the kids' lunches for this week?
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant on someone's phone. Help with what they ask. When you plan meals, put two days on each line and start the line with those days.

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Plan lunches for Mia and Leo this week
pieces.text: Plan school lunches for my two kids, Mia and Leo, for this week.

slots.label: What does Pipo need to know?

pieces.label: No school on Friday
pieces.text: There's no school on Friday, so only Monday to Thursday.

pieces.label: Each lunch takes 10 minutes or less
pieces.text: Each lunch has to take 10 minutes or less to make.

pieces.label: Make them super fancy!
pieces.tip: "Super fancy" sounds fun, but fancy takes time you don't have on a school morning.

pieces.label: Explain all about healthy eating
pieces.text: Explain everything about healthy eating for kids.
pieces.tip: A lecture isn't a lunch plan. Asking for something short gets you a list you can shop from.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo the kids are vegetarian.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know the kids are vegetarian, so there's meat in the lunches.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo there's no school on Friday.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know Friday is a day off, so it planned a lunch nobody needs.

flaws.hint: "Help me with lunches" doesn't say who they're for, so Pipo has to guess.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know who the lunches are for, so it guessed.

lesson: Tell Pipo the limits that matter: allergies, and which days you actually need.
